name: ShopFlow Architecture
description: Memory palace for the ShopFlow e-commerce platform architecture

loci.name: Station Airlock
loci.description: The entry point to the station. Red and green lights indicate system status. A holographic welcome screen shows the ShopFlow logo.

memories.subject: System Overview
memories.image: A 3D HOLOGRAM of the entire station SPINS before you as you enter. Each module PULSES with activity - orders flowing like GLOWING PARTICLES between sections. A friendly AI voice announces: 'Welcome to ShopFlow Station: Microservices Architecture, 12 services, 3 databases, serving 10M requests/day!'
memories.content: ShopFlow is a microservices-based e-commerce platform with 12 independent services, 3 specialized databases (PostgreSQL for users, MongoDB for products, Redis for sessions), handling 10M daily requests.

loci.name: Command Bridge
loci.description: The nerve center with a massive viewport showing data streams like stars. Multiple control stations surround the captain's chair.

memories.subject: API Gateway
memories.image: The CAPTAIN'S CHAIR is actually a giant ROUTER - the captain IS the API Gateway! Every request BEAMS IN through the viewport as a colored light. The captain CATCHES each one and THROWS it to the correct station. Rate limiting shields DEFLECT too many requests from one source.
memories.content: Kong API Gateway handles all incoming traffic. Routes to appropriate microservice. Implements rate limiting (1000 req/min per user), JWT validation, and request logging.

memories.subject: Authentication Flow
memories.image: A FINGERPRINT SCANNER at the bridge entrance that creates GLOWING TOKENS. Each token is a tiny SPACESHIP that follows the user around. The token spaceship must DOCK at each service or ALARMS blare. Tokens EXPIRE and CRUMBLE TO DUST after 1 hour.
memories.content: JWT-based auth with 1-hour expiry. Refresh tokens stored in Redis (7-day expiry). Auth service issues tokens, all other services validate via shared public key.

loci.name: Engineering Deck
loci.anchor: humming reactor core visible through floor grating
loci.description: The heart of the station. Pipes and conduits run everywhere. Engineers in orange suits monitor pulsing displays.

memories.subject: Order Processing Service
memories.image: A massive ASSEMBLY LINE where order ROBOTS grab products from conveyor belts. Each robot has a STATE MACHINE brain - it can only be in one state: PENDING (yellow), PROCESSING (blue), SHIPPED (green), or CANCELLED (red). State transitions require PROPER PAPERWORK or the robot REFUSES.
memories.content: Order service uses state machine pattern. States: PENDING → PAYMENT_PROCESSING → CONFIRMED → SHIPPED → DELIVERED (or CANCELLED from any state). Kafka events trigger transitions.

memories.subject: Event-Driven Architecture
memories.image: PNEUMATIC TUBES connecting every section of the station! Messages WHOOSH through as colored capsules. KAFKA is a giant octopus in the center, catching capsules with tentacles and redirecting them. Each tentacle is labeled with a topic: 'orders', 'inventory', 'notifications'.
memories.content: Kafka message bus connects all services. Topics: orders, inventory-updates, user-events, notifications. Each service publishes events and subscribes to relevant topics. At-least-once delivery guaranteed.

loci.name: Power Core
loci.description: The deepest part of engineering. A massive cylindrical reactor hums with energy. Control panels show performance metrics.

memories.subject: Caching Strategy
memories.image: A CRYSTAL BALL that REMEMBERS everything it's shown. When you ask it a question, it checks its memory FIRST (cache hit = instant glow). If it doesn't know, it sends a MESSENGER to the database (cache miss = waiting). The crystal has a CLEANING GNOME that wipes old memories every 5 minutes.
memories.content: Redis caching layer. Strategy: Cache-aside pattern. Product data cached 5min TTL, user sessions cached until expiry, search results cached 1min. Cache invalidation on writes via Kafka events.

loci.name: Cargo Hold
loci.description: Zero-gravity cargo bay with containers floating in organized sections. Robots zip between them moving products.

memories.subject: Product Database (MongoDB)
memories.image: SHAPE-SHIFTING CONTAINERS that can hold ANYTHING. Unlike rigid boxes, these containers MORPH to fit whatever you put in them. Products with different attributes? No problem - the container ADAPTS. They're organized in COLLECTIONS (aisles) and have INDEXES (robot fast-travel tubes).
memories.content: MongoDB stores products. Schema-flexible for varying product attributes. Collections: products, categories, reviews. Indexes on: productId, categoryId, name (text), price. Sharded by categoryId for horizontal scaling.

memories.subject: User Database (PostgreSQL)
memories.image: A MASSIVE FILING CABINET made of ADAMANTIUM - unbreakable and perfectly organized. Each drawer has EXACTLY the same structure. Try to put something in the wrong format? The drawer SPITS IT BACK. ACID-BREATHING DRAGONS guard the cabinet - they ensure Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability!
memories.content: PostgreSQL for users, orders, payments. ACID compliance critical for financial data. Tables: users, addresses, orders, order_items, payments. Foreign key relationships enforced. Read replicas for scaling queries.

loci.name: Communications Array
loci.anchor: massive satellite dishes and blinking antennae
loci.description: The external communication hub. Dishes point in all directions. Screens show real-time message traffic.

memories.subject: External API Design
memories.image: A UNIVERSAL TRANSLATOR station where internal station language gets converted to EXTERNAL LANGUAGE (REST). Every response is wrapped in a STANDARD ENVELOPE: { data, errors, meta }. Version numbers are painted on DIFFERENT FREQUENCIES - v1 on channel 1, v2 on channel 2.
memories.content: REST API with versioning (/api/v1/, /api/v2/). Standard response format: { data: T, errors: Error[], meta: { page, totalPages } }. OpenAPI spec auto-generated. Breaking changes only in major versions.

memories.subject: Third-Party Integrations
memories.image: EMBASSY ROOMS for different alien species (third parties). STRIPE aliens handle payments in a secure vault. SENDGRID aliens handle email - they have MESSENGER BIRDS. TWILIO aliens do SMS - they have LOUD SPEAKERS. Each embassy has its own QUARANTINE PROTOCOL (circuit breaker).
memories.content: Integrations: Stripe (payments), SendGrid (email), Twilio (SMS), AWS S3 (images). Each wrapped in adapter pattern with circuit breaker (30s timeout, 5 failures = open). Fallback queues for retries.
